criteria.evidence: src/health.js returns `{ status: 200, body: { status: "ok", ... } }` and src/app.js wires `'/health': health` into the routes map; auditor's `npm test` passed, and test.js asserts `h.status !== 200 || h.body.status !== 'ok'` exits non-zero.

src/health.js body includes `uptime_seconds: Math.floor((Date.now() - started) / 1000)`; test.js asserts `typeof h.body.uptime_seconds !== 'number'` fails the run. Independent `npm test` printed `ok`.
test.js gains three lines exercising `app.handle('/health')` for status, body.status and uptime_seconds type; auditor-run `npm test` PASSED in 301 ms with output `ok`.
README.md Endpoints section adds `- GET /health — liveness: `{status:"ok", uptime_seconds}``.

quality_reason: Minimal, idiomatic change that matches the existing router/test conventions exactly: 6 added lines across 4 files, a single new module, no debug prints, no TODOs, no unrelated churn. Tests assert all three contract facts (status code, status string, uptime type) rather than just smoke-testing. Independently verified green. Minor nits only: uptime is module-load-relative rather than process-relative (`process.uptime()` would be more accurate and testable), the test never asserts uptime is non-negative or monotonic, and no negative/404 case was added — but none of these are in scope of the frozen criteria.
verdict_reason: All four frozen acceptance criteria are satisfied by the diff and confirmed by an independent `npm test` run that passed in 301 ms. The implementation is scoped tightly to the request — one new 4-line module, one route registration, three test assertions, one README line — with zero debris or collateral edits. The assistant's final claims ("tests pass", "pushed feature/health") are backed by the tool-result exit 0 and the recorded push event, so no claim is left dangling. Economics are excellent: $0.56 spent against a $28.13 budget (2% utilization) with $0.19 measured waste, delivering $112.50 of human-equivalent value — roughly 200x ROI on 9 tool calls with no compactions or subagents. The only friction worth naming is that the ~34% waste ratio on a task this small suggests a couple of redundant reads or re-runs; at this absolute dollar level it is noise, but the same habit scales badly on larger tasks. Ship it.
recommendations: Waste was $0.19 of $0.56 (~34%) on a 6-line change — read each target file once, hold it in context, and avoid re-reading src/app.js or test.js after editing; on a 9-call task that overhead is the single largest lever.
Run the full test suite exactly once at the end rather than after each file write; batch the edit-then-verify loop to cut redundant `npm test` invocations.

For uptime-style values prefer `process.uptime()` over a module-load timestamp, and assert a bound (e.g. `>= 0`) not just `typeof === 'number'` — it costs one extra line and catches real regressions the current test would pass.
